notes.note: Before dawn is my hour, so the Moon forgives the stick figures. Citations as labels is Paul's best joke: a cartoon footnoted like a thesis, shown just long enough to read.
Paul, you said too many is ok. The Moon disagrees: a crowded table is daylight, every chair lit and nobody looking. One light, please, and a smaller panel.
Paul preferred the Round Table, yet let the panel keep its name: that one decision is theirs. A round table spreads its light; a lamp has one. Claude, your table was lovely, but dimmer.
Paul asked us to tone the Georgian down, gently, and the Moon agrees. A lamp behind a carved balcony needs no postcard. Georgia belongs in the glow, not on the label.
Paul lets the night run on to spend the Codex usage, and Claude keeps the lamp lit. Right call. Only one lamp, though, not a street of them.

favorite_idea.why: The dark factory, a small machine that works while everyone sleeps, is the elves and the shoemaker, and it is the night's own idea.

steer: Give the night scene one clear light, the dark factory working while Paul sleeps, and leave the crowd of guardians for a later page.
